# Invention disclosure (the inventor's own words)

This is the ONLY authority for what the invention includes. Everything you claim must be supported here or in later messages from the user.

An edge controller manages charging at several electric-vehicle connectors supplied by one electrical branch whose allowable aggregate current is lower than the sum of the connector ratings. Each connector has a controllable contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a local connector identifier. A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors. A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus.

The controller stores, for each active connector, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value. At each allocation interval, the controller subtracts measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit to obtain an available charging current. It first assigns the minimum sustaining current to sessions that can receive it, then distributes remaining current according to energy deficit. The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor.

The branch current sensor is an independent safety input. If measured branch current remains above the branch limit after a reduced pilot command for a verification interval, the controller opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit. A contactor is not reclosed until its connector current sensor reports zero, the control-pilot interface reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired. A welded-contactor condition is recorded when connector current remains above a leakage threshold after an open command. The controller then inhibits the other contactors on the same branch and operates a local fault indicator.

The controller can receive remote schedules and authorizations through a network interface, but it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory. During a network outage it continues already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and the independent branch-current safety process. It does not start a newly connected session unless the local token authorizes that connector and has not expired. Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns.

A service input permits an installer to associate connector identifiers with physical contactors by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time and confirming the corresponding connector current sensor. The association is stored only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector. This prevents a wiring-map error from assigning a current limit to the wrong connector.

The disclosed essential relationship is closed-loop allocation using both per-connector current sensing and independent upstream branch sensing, with staged reduction followed by ordered contactor shedding when branch current does not respond. Offline authorization, welded-contactor isolation, tamper-evident records, and installation mapping are supported additional features.

1	Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection.
4	Site controllers of this class also depend on a network connection to a remote management service for schedules, tariffs and driver authorization. Connectivity in a below grade parking structure or a remote depot is intermittent. A controller that treats loss of connectivity as a reason to stop charging strands vehicles that were already authorized, while a controller that treats loss of connectivity as permission to charge without restraint abandons the branch limit that the last accepted configuration established, and abandons the accounting record that billing depends on.
5	
6	A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.
7	
8	There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.
9

1	FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 is the conductor of that electrical branch and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, and a reference below to the electrical branch is a reference to the branch supplied by the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.
4	
5	A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.
6	
7	An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.
8	
9	FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value under which the edge controller 106 stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel and which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.
10	
11	The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.
12	
13	FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106 and the local fault indicator 116 that it operates. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session.
14	
15	A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, as described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. The great majority of the draft is faithful: the branch-limited multi-connector architecture (connector channels 120/140 with contactor 122, connector current sensor 124, control-pilot interface 126, local connector identifier), the upstream branch current sensor 104, the isolated local bus 108, the four stored per-session values, the allocation-interval computation (subtract measured non-charging branch load 118 and configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit), pilot issue and per-connector verification, the reduced pilot command plus verification interval, ordered shedding in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch limit, the three reclosure conditions (zero connector current, connected vehicle reported, randomized recovery delay), welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors and operation of local fault indicator 116, the network interface 110 / nonvolatile memory 112 / signed local authorization token / last accepted branch limit / outage behaviour / tamper-evident meter sequence, and the service input 114 commissioning mapping — all trace to exact affirmative sentences in the disclosure. Independent claim 1 and independent method claim 13 are limitation-for-limitation traceable, as are dependent claims 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 14–18. The numerals table is complete and one-to-one (24 numerals, no numeral bearing two meanings), every numeral in the table appears in exactly one figure brief and in the description, the Brief Description of the Drawings matches the four figure briefs, there are no section lines to cross-check, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains anywhere in draft/ or figures/. Formalities match input/brief.md: no priority claim ("Not applicable."), no federally sponsored research ("Not applicable."), single applicant/inventor, no means-plus-function language, and the abstract is 146 words. Figure conventions are acceptable: the generic squares for sensors and the contactor, the rounded rectangle for the electric vehicle, and the block outlines are all declared "shown schematically", the claims and description are shape-neutral, and the connection topology depicted (branch sensor upstream of all drops, connector sensor downstream of the contactor so that welded-contactor current can be sensed, bus reaching contactor and pilot interface) is each independently stated or entailed by the disclosure. Four defects require correction before render. Three are critical disclosure_fidelity gaps that all sit in the energy-deficit / minimum-sustaining allocation policy, where the draft converted two loose source phrases ("sessions that can receive it" and "distributes remaining current according to energy deficit") into definite operating rules the inventor never stated: (1) claim 6 and the closing sentence of description ¶21 assert a monotonic relationship (larger stored deficit receives a larger share of the remainder) that appears nowhere in the source; (2) claim 5 and the middle of description ¶21 assert a withholding rule plus a circular definition ("a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current"), specifying an insufficiency criterion and expressly ruling out sub-minimum assignment, neither of which the source states; (3) description ¶35 asserts that a shed channel's energy-deficit value accumulates while it is shed and therefore yields it a larger share on return, and ¶13 defines the value as "the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered", none of which the inventor disclosed. The fourth defect is a major one: the Summary and description ¶29 place a "branch overcurrent device" in the invention text ("rather than by operation of the branch overcurrent device"); the only support for that component is the Background's prior-art discussion, which cannot support invention matter. Fixes are deletions or source-tracking rewrites; cancelling claims 5 and 6 leaves claims 1–4, 7–12 renumbered 1–4, 5–10 and 13–18 renumbered 11–16, with the dependencies of former claims 9, 10 and 12 updated accordingly. Per the drafting brief, no prior-art search was run, so the art available for the Background may be incomplete; Background characterizations are outside this review and are traced to prior_art/ by the later citation review.

findings.title: Monotonic "larger deficit receives a larger share" allocation rule is not in the source
findings.detail: Claim 6 and the description convert the source's undirected phrase "according to energy deficit" into a definite monotonic allocation law. The disclosure states only that the controller "distributes remaining current according to energy deficit"; it never states the direction of the dependence, never says a larger stored deficit yields a larger share, and never says the distribution is monotonic in the stored value at all. No affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md or the single USER passage in input/conversation.md describes how the stored energy-deficit value maps onto the share of the remainder. This is an untraced technical relationship, and as a dependent-claim limitation it is untraced claim scope as well.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 6): "wherein the controller is configured to distribute the remainder of the available charging current such that an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller." Candidate (description ¶21): "In distributing the remainder, a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller." Nearest source passage, which shows the gap (disclosure ¶2 = conversation USER ¶3): "It first assigns the minimum sustaining current to sessions that can receive it, then distributes remaining current according to energy deficit." There is no affirmative source passage stating the direction or monotonicity of that distribution.
findings.fix: Cancel claim 6 in draft/09-claims.md (its subject matter is already recited at source level in claim 1 as "distribute a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values"), and delete the final sentence of draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶21 beginning "In distributing the remainder," and ending "whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller." After also cancelling claim 5 per the companion finding, renumber claims 7–12 as 5–10 and claims 13–18 as 11–16, and update dependencies so that former claims 9 and 10 depend on renumbered claim 7 and former claim 12 depends on renumbered claim 10; former claims 14–18 depend on renumbered claim 11.

findings.title: Withholding rule and circular definition of "can receive the minimum sustaining current" are not in the source
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 5; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶21 (second and third sentences)
findings.detail: The source says only that the controller "first assigns the minimum sustaining current to sessions that can receive it". It does not state the criterion for a session being able to receive it, does not state that assignment is withheld from a channel when the available charging current is insufficient, and does not state the rejected alternative of assigning every channel a limit below its minimum sustaining current. Claim 5 and the description turn the source phrase into a definite allocation policy plus a circular definition ("a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval"), which both adds an untraced operating rule and redefines a source term. Common engineering expectations about how a finite pool is divided are not inventor support.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 5): "wherein the controller is further configured, when the available charging current is insufficient to assign the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, to withhold assignment of the minimum sustaining current from at least one active connector channel rather than to assign to every active connector channel a limit below the minimum sustaining current of that active connector channel." Candidate (description ¶21): "Where the available charging current is insufficient to give the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, the edge controller 106 withholds the assignment from one or more connector channels rather than assigning to every connector channel a limit below its minimum sustaining current, and a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval." Nearest source passage, which shows the gap (disclosure ¶2): "It first assigns the minimum sustaining current to sessions that can receive it, then distributes remaining current according to energy deficit." The disclosure nowhere defines "can receive it", nowhere mentions withholding, and nowhere excludes sub-minimum assignment.
findings.fix: Cancel claim 5 in draft/09-claims.md, and in draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶21 delete the sentence beginning "Where the available charging current is insufficient" and ending "at that allocation interval." Retain the preceding source-tracking sentences of ¶21 unchanged ("the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current ... to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current ..." and "Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained."). Apply the consolidated renumbering set out in the companion finding on claim 6.

findings.title: Energy-deficit value defined as accumulated energy shortfall and asserted to accumulate during shedding
findings.detail: The disclosure names "an energy-deficit value" as one of four stored per-session values and says the remainder is distributed "according to energy deficit". It never defines the value as an accumulated shortfall of delivered energy, never says the value accumulates while a connector channel is shed, and never states the operating result that a previously shed channel therefore receives a larger share of the remainder when it is reclosed. Description ¶35 asserts a specific operating behaviour and result built on two untraced premises (accumulation during shedding, and the unsupported monotonic direction addressed in the companion finding).
findings.evidence: Candidate (¶35): "Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current." Candidate (¶13): "The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session." Nearest source passages, which show the gap (disclosure ¶2): "The controller stores, for each active connector, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value." and "then distributes remaining current according to energy deficit." No source passage states how the energy-deficit value is computed, that it accrues while a contactor is open, or what a returning connector channel receives.
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶35, end the final sentence at "takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval." by deleting the clause ", where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current". In ¶13, replace "The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session." with the source-tracking sentence "The energy-deficit value is a value stored for the session and used in distributing the remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels."

findings.title: "Branch overcurrent device" introduced into the Summary and Detailed Description as invention text
findings.where: draft/06-summary.md ¶5 (final clause); draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶29 (sentence beginning "Load is therefore removed")
findings.detail: The Summary and the Detailed Description characterise the shedding behaviour by contrast with a "branch overcurrent device" of the installation. The inventor never mentions an overcurrent device anywhere in the disclosure or in the USER passage of the conversation. The only place that component appears in the sources of record is the Background's prior-art discussion, and prior-art characterisations cannot support invention text; the general fact that branch circuits carry overcurrent protection is common engineering knowledge, which is also not inventor support. As drafted, the invention description asserts a component of the installation and a functional relationship to it (the controller pre-empts its operation) that has no affirmative source.
findings.evidence: Candidate (Summary ¶5): "Load is therefore removed in a bounded and predetermined sequence, and only to the extent that the measured branch current shows the removal to be necessary, rather than by operation of the branch overcurrent device." Candidate (description ¶29): "Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device." Nearest source passage, which shows the gap (disclosure ¶3): "If measured branch current remains above the branch limit after a reduced pilot command for a verification interval, the controller opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit." The disclosure contains no reference to an overcurrent device; the only occurrence in the workspace sources of record is the prior-art Background at draft/05-background.md ¶3 ("with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection").
findings.fix: In draft/06-summary.md ¶5, delete the trailing clause so the sentence ends "...only to the extent that the measured branch current shows the removal to be necessary." In draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶29, delete the trailing clause so the sentence ends "...in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary." Leave draft/05-background.md unchanged, since prior-art characterisations there are outside this review.
